title: Kyle Shanahan: Brock Purdy's ankle sprain is "more mid than low"
summary: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy emerged from Sunday's win over the Vikings with an ankle injury.
content: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy emerged from Sunday's win over the Vikings with an ankle injury. He'll miss Sunday's game against the Seahawks. Whether he'll miss any games beyond that remains to be seen. “It's too soon, but I'm pretty optimistic about it," coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Friday. "But, I was about this week to start and then it changes, so hopefully it'll be all right.” Next Sunday, the 49ers visit the Giants. The following weekend, the Rams visit. Shanahan also revealed some details about the specific nature of the ankle sprain. “Anytime it's not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse," Shanahan said. "Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. Didn't heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down.” Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy. Purdy's performance in 2026 has made him one of the favorites to win the NFL MVP award.

title: Mike Macdonald on Sam Darnold, when healthy: "I think he's done a good job"
summary: Quarterback Sam Darnold is back as Seattle's starter this week, after missing two games due to quad and rib injuries.
content: Quarterback Sam Darnold is back as Seattle's starter this week, after missing two games due to quad and rib injuries. It's an opportunity to improve on what has been a challenging start to the 2026 season. On Friday, coach Mike Macdonald was asked to assess Darnold's performance when healthy. "I think he’s done a good job," Macdonald said. "As a football team, we’ve been good enough to go 6-4, and we want to get better. Yeah, he’s right there with everybody else.” Well, he's not right there with the player who replaced him. Drew Lock has started three games and played all but one drive of another. His record is 4-0. Darnold is 2-4. And their numbers are starkly different. Darnold has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions. Lock has thrown seven touchdown passes and no interceptions. Lock's passer rating is 125.6. Darnold's is 79.5. Lock's games have come against the Patriots, the Cardinals twice, and the Raiders. Darnold has faced the Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, and Bears — a much tougher slate of opponents. The Seahawks won a Super Bowl with Darnold. That counts for something. Still, they're 6-4. They have an opportunity to get a seventh win on Sunday, with Brock Purdy out for the game against the 49ers.

title: Mike McCarthy admits he hasn't spent enough time with the defense
summary: McCarthy vows to take a closer look at the situation in the offseason.
content: After registering an unlikely 27-5 win over the previously 8-2 Broncos, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn't angry, resentful, or defiant. He was the same guy he always is, and he admitted that (as former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said this week), McCarthy hasn't been sufficiently invested in the side of the ball that isn't his personal expertise. "I have not spent enough time with the defense ," McCarthy told reporters. "You know, and that’s something that, as far as job responsibility, job description, you know, these are things that'll be looked at in the offseason. But, you know, it’s a point in our year where we’re making adjustments and definitely conscientious of it. But at the end of the day, we have to all do our jobs and make sure we're giving the players the plan and all the other things that they need that we can perform and play with that type of urgency, physicality that we played today.” McCarthy prefaced his comments with a lesson he learned as a boy, growing up in Pittsburgh. "My father used to tell me all the time as a kid, 'You tell the truth, you only have to tell your story once,'" McCarthy said. The truth is that this week has entailed two sharply different versions of reality, where both things can indeed be the truth. One, McCarthy (like all of us) has flaws. Two, Rodgers should not have spoken about them publicly. Rodgers clumsily defended his decision to break the code of a football locker room by texting this to Al Michaels: “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership." That's fine, but how does disregarding the "sanctity" of the locker room (a word Rodgers undoubtedly selected in response to Tom Brady using it on Thursday ) create "accountability"? McCarthy is accountable to team owner Art Rooney II. Not to the media or the fans. Also, who decides when breaking the code is justified in the name of "accountability" to people to whom McCarthy isn't directly accountable? There's no tribunal to whom Rodgers can apply for permission to disregard the privacy of a football team's inner workings. He took it on himself. And to what end? He was either doing it to help the Steelers save their season, or he was lashing out. We'll let you decide which explanation is more likely.
